topic: Evolution and inheritance: adaptation and natural selection
subject: Science

answers.objectiveVerb: Explain how living things adapt and evolve

objectives.text: Define adaptation as a feature that helps a living thing survive in its environment
Describe how an adaptation helps an animal or plant survive in its environment
Explain how natural selection can make useful adaptations more common over generations

keyIdeas.statement: An adaptation is a feature that helps a living thing survive in its environment.
keyIdeas.explanation: A feature can be a body part, body covering or behaviour. It helps the living thing meet its needs, such as finding food, staying safe or coping with conditions.
keyIdeas.example: A polar bear's thick fur is a feature that helps it survive in the cold Arctic environment.

keyIdeas.statement: An adaptation is useful because it suits the environment where the living thing lives.
keyIdeas.explanation: The same feature may not be useful everywhere. A feature is an adaptation when it helps a particular living thing survive in its own surroundings and conditions.
keyIdeas.example: The waxy coating on a holly leaf helps the plant survive in the damp woodlands of Britain.

keyIdeas.statement: An adaptation helps a living thing meet a need in its environment.
keyIdeas.explanation: It may help an animal get food, stay safe, keep warm, or avoid losing water. The feature is useful because it suits the conditions where the living thing lives.
keyIdeas.example: A polar bear's thick fur traps warm air, helping it keep warm in the cold Arctic environment.

keyIdeas.statement: One adaptation can help in more than one way.
keyIdeas.explanation: A feature may help a living thing survive by finding food and avoiding danger, or by saving water and protecting it from other animals.
keyIdeas.example: A cactus has spines instead of broad leaves. This helps it lose less water in a hot desert and makes it harder for animals to eat.

keyIdeas.statement: Natural selection makes a useful inherited feature more common over generations.
keyIdeas.explanation: Offspring vary. If a feature helps some living things survive and reproduce, they are more likely to pass that feature to their offspring. After many generations, more of the population may have it.
keyIdeas.example: During the nineteenth-century Industrial Revolution in England, dark peppered moths were harder for birds to see on soot-darkened tree trunks, so dark moths became more common in some polluted areas.

keyIdeas.statement: Natural selection acts on differences that already exist in a population.
keyIdeas.explanation: A living thing does not choose to develop a useful feature because it needs one. Individuals with a helpful inherited difference are more likely to survive and reproduce, so the difference can spread through the population.
keyIdeas.example: Peppered moths were not all the same colour; birds were more likely to eat the moths that stood out against the tree trunks.

misconceptions.belief: A living thing chooses to develop a useful feature when it needs one.
misconceptions.correction: An adaptation is an existing feature that helps survival. Living things do not choose or instantly grow adaptations because they need them.

misconceptions.belief: An adaptation helps a living thing because it chooses to develop or practise that feature.
misconceptions.correction: An adaptation is a feature an organism has. It helps because the feature suits its environment; the organism does not choose to grow it when needed.

misconceptions.belief: An animal changes its body during its lifetime because it needs a feature, then passes that change to its offspring.
misconceptions.correction: Natural selection starts with inherited differences between offspring. Those with a helpful difference are more likely to survive and reproduce, so the difference becomes more common over many generations.

vocabulary.definition: A feature that helps a living thing survive in its environment.
The surroundings and conditions in which a living thing lives.
Colours or patterns that make a living thing harder to see in its surroundings.
A layer or covering that slows heat moving into or out of something.
Differences between individuals of the same kind of living thing.
A group of offspring born at about the same time, or the step from parents to their offspring.

workedExamples.problem: Suppose some beetles are brown and some are green. On brown tree bark, explain how brown colouring could become more common over generations.
steps: There is variation: some beetles are brown and some are green.
Birds eat more of the green beetles because they are easier to see.
More brown beetles survive and reproduce than green beetles.
Their offspring may inherit brown colouring, so brown beetles become more common over generations.
workedExamples.answer: Brown colouring becomes more common because brown beetles survive and reproduce more often, passing the inherited feature to offspring.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly defines an adaptation?
questions.answer: A feature that helps a living thing survive in its environment.
questions.reasoning: An adaptation is a useful feature that suits the surroundings where the living thing lives.

distractors.text: A place where an animal lives
A change a living thing chooses to make
Any feature that all living things share

questions.stem: Complete the definition: An adaptation is a feature that helps a living thing…
questions.reasoning: The feature must help the living thing survive in its particular surroundings and conditions.

distractors.text: change its environment
choose its parents
become a different species immediately

questions.stem: A cactus has a thick, waxy outer covering. Which statement best identifies this as an adaptation?
questions.answer: It is a feature that helps the cactus survive in its environment.
questions.reasoning: The covering is a feature of the cactus and helps it live in its surroundings.

distractors.text: It is a place where the cactus grows
It is a feature the cactus chose to grow
It is a feature that every plant must have

questions.answer: A duck's webbed feet help it swim in ponds and lakes.
questions.reasoning: Webbed feet are a feature that helps the duck survive in its watery environment.

distractors.text: A duck swims in a pond
A duck decides to grow webbed feet
A pond is where a duck lives

questions.stem: Which statement best describes how a polar bear's thick fur helps it survive?
questions.answer: It traps warm air, helping the polar bear keep warm in the cold Arctic.
questions.reasoning: The fur suits the cold conditions by slowing heat loss.

distractors.text: It helps the polar bear swim faster.
It makes the polar bear need no food.
It makes the Arctic warmer.

questions.stem: Describe how cactus spines help a cactus survive in a hot desert.
questions.answer: They are small instead of broad leaves, so less water escapes, and they can deter animals from eating the cactus.
questions.reasoning: The spines suit a dry environment by reducing water loss and offering protection.

distractors.text: They collect all the cactus's food from the air.
They make the cactus walk to water.
They give the cactus broad leaves for shade.

questions.stem: A fish has a streamlined body. Describe how this adaptation helps it survive in water.
questions.answer: Its shape reduces resistance from the water, helping it move efficiently to find food or escape danger.
questions.reasoning: A streamlined shape makes movement through water easier.

distractors.text: It allows the fish to breathe air on land.
It makes the water warmer around the fish.
It stops the fish needing to find food.

questions.stem: Explain why camouflage can help a prey animal survive.
questions.answer: Camouflage makes the animal harder for predators to see, so it is less likely to be caught and eaten.
questions.reasoning: The colour or pattern suits the animal's surroundings and helps it avoid danger.

distractors.text: It makes the animal invisible everywhere.
It gives the animal more energy.
It means predators cannot see any animals.

questions.stem: Which sequence best explains how a useful inherited feature becomes more common?
questions.answer: Variation, different survival and reproduction, then more offspring inherit the feature.
questions.reasoning: Existing differences affect survival and reproduction, so inherited useful features can spread over generations.

distractors.text: Need, change during life, then pass on the change.
All individuals change in the same way at once.
The environment directly gives every individual the feature.

questions.stem: Suppose darker mice are harder for owls to see on dark soil. Explain why dark fur may become more common.
questions.answer: Dark mice are more likely to survive and reproduce, so they may pass dark fur to more offspring over generations.
questions.reasoning: Being harder to see increases the chance of surviving long enough to reproduce.

distractors.text: The mice choose to grow darker fur.
Owls change the mice's genes by hunting them.
Every mouse becomes dark during its lifetime.

questions.stem: Why must offspring vary for natural selection to make an adaptation more common?
questions.answer: Without differences, some individuals would not have a feature that gives them a survival or reproduction advantage.
questions.reasoning: Natural selection needs inherited differences for survival and reproduction to differ.

distractors.text: Variation makes all offspring identical.
Variation means an animal chooses its features.
Variation stops features being inherited.

questions.stem: A drought leaves only hard seeds for finches. Some have thicker beaks, and this difference is inherited. Explain how thicker beaks could become more common.
questions.answer: Finches with thicker beaks may eat more, survive and reproduce more, passing the inherited beak shape to more offspring over generations.
questions.reasoning: The food supply favours a heritable difference that helps finches survive and reproduce.

distractors.text: Finches grow thicker beaks because they need them.
All finches develop thick beaks in one generation.
Thin-beaked finches choose to have no offspring.
